update_from: User-provided screenshot captured 2026-09-05. Rates are transcribed from that screenshot and have not been independently source-validated. Plan prices remain separately sourced from https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing.
model_ids_note: The Astra/Sol/Terra/Luna orchestration and worker ids match the Codex runtime roster captured in this session. GPT-5.5 is runtime-available but cost-only for this policy. GPT-5.4 nano is transcribed from the pricing screenshot and was absent from the runtime roster (which listed a distinct GPT-5.4 mini), so nano is marked unavailable and cost-only. codex-auto-review remains a non-selectable observed id with an explicitly assumed rate.

api.note: Token-metered API cost estimates (OPENAI_API_KEY auth) use the per-model rates and provenance recorded below; screenshot-transcribed and assumed rates are labeled accordingly.

subscription.note: Codex CLI under a ChatGPT plan (ChatGPT sign-in) draws down opaque usage/rate limits, not dollars. OpenAI publishes no token-to-quota conversion: any dollar figure shown for a subscription run is an API-equivalent relative-burn proxy and must be labeled as such — never presented as a bill. GPT-5.6 is GA across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API (announcement, 2026-07-18 capture); plan-level limits remain unpublished — never fabricate an allowance.

cache_note: Explicit cached-input and cache-write rates are stored per model and per threshold tier. The multipliers remain for backward compatibility with historical consumers; new cost calculations use the explicit rates.
long_context_note: A long-context tier applies only when one request's input-token count exceeds that model's threshold. Aggregate task-profile or session totals must not trigger it unless explicitly identified as a single request.

plus.note: Usage-limited; no published token allowance exists — never fabricate one.

pro.note: Higher limits than Plus; still no published token allowance.

knobs.reasoning_efforts_note: Union of reasoning efforts reported by the local Codex runtime model/list probe on 2026-09-05. Supported levels vary by model; consult each model's supported_reasoning_efforts.

ultra.note: Reported by the local Codex runtime as a supported reasoning effort for Astra, Sol, and Terra, with automatic task delegation; Luna does not report support. No pricing multiplier is inferred.

fast.note: Codex fast mode: priority processing for time-sensitive work — the published speed lever. CLI surface and pricing impact unpublished as of cached_date — no flag or multiplier invented.

gpt-6-astra.notes: Reserved orchestration and evidence-gated recovery model; excluded from ordinary implementation and routine verification.

gpt-5.6-sol.notes: Difficult implementation, security-sensitive work, complex integration, and independent verification.

gpt-5.5.notes: Cost-only entry; not eligible for Polytropos worker routing.

gpt-5.4-nano.notes: Cost-only entry; not eligible for Polytropos worker routing.

codex-auto-review.notes: Codex Desktop's automatic code-review feature (rollout originator 'Codex Desktop'), observed in ~/.codex logs. Opaque id: rollouts expose no backing model, so it is NOT user-selectable and NOT a routing target — tier 'non-routing' is outside the cheap|mid|strong|frontier vocabulary and is skipped by resolve_tier. Rates are an ASSUMED best-effort equal to GPT-5.3-Codex (doc-confirmed $1.75/$0.175/$14.00 per the 2026-07-10 OpenAI pricing table) so the daily journal can price it as a labeled API-equivalent proxy — never authoritative; correct or remove if the true backing model/rate is confirmed.

tier_note: Codex routing uses cheap|mid|strong workers plus a reserved frontier orchestrator. Cost-only and non-routing entries are never selected for work.
